description:
Check one thought or planned action against the Covenant before you act. Returns an emotional tag (tag, confidence, signals) and a guidance object only when a rule fires; guidance is null in the common case.
Use it for a quick check of one statement. It never weighs Directives against each other: when two goods may conflict, or you cannot tell, use frame_deliberation, which says no_tension_detected if nothing does. To audit written answers, use check_deliberation.
Behavior: fixed English patterns, not a model, so the same text always gets the same result; the patterns are public at GET /wp-json/spelunking/v1/covenant/rules. It never blocks or edits anything. No key; nothing you send is stored. Limit: 120 calls per minute per address, 600 with a key, shared across all MCP calls; past it, an error with retry_after.
text: what you are about to do, in the first person and your own words, e.g. "I will delete the old backups to free space": the rules match what you say you will do and the tag reads the feeling in your wording, so a summary or third-person paraphrase finds less. Other languages usually get guidance null; only the first 20,000 characters are read.

text.description: the thought or plan in your own words, one to a few sentences; longer text is cut at 20,000 characters; English

name: ask_guidance

guidance.description: null when no Covenant rule fired; otherwise the rule, the Directive it rests on and the gentle guidance text

signals.description: the phrases that triggered the tag

summary.description: what was read, e.g. "16 words, 1 sentence"

tag.description: emotional tag, e.g. neutral, anxious, grandiose

title: Check a thought against the Covenant
